questions.question: Which structure is the primary female sex organ?
questions.explanation: The ovaries are the female gonads; they produce ova and female sex hormones.
questions.miniGuide: The ovaries are the female gonads; they produce ova and female sex hormones.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: What is the main role of the broad, ovarian, and suspensory ligaments?
questions.explanation: These ligaments stabilize the ovaries within the pelvic cavity.
questions.miniGuide: These ligaments stabilize the ovaries within the pelvic cavity.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: Which uterine layer is the usual site of blastocyst implantation?
questions.explanation: The endometrium is the inner uterine lining that changes during the cycle and receives the implanting blastocyst.
questions.miniGuide: The endometrium is the inner uterine lining that changes during the cycle and receives the implanting blastocyst.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: Strong uterine contractions during labor depend mainly on which layer?
questions.explanation: The myometrium is the thick smooth-muscle layer that provides most uterine contractile force.
questions.miniGuide: The myometrium is the thick smooth-muscle layer that provides most uterine contractile force.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: Where does fertilization most commonly occur?

choices.A: Upper third of a fallopian tube

questions.explanation: The lecture identifies the upper third of the fallopian tube as the usual site of fertilization.
questions.miniGuide: The lecture identifies the upper third of the fallopian tube as the usual site of fertilization.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: Which pair of mechanisms moves an ovum through a fallopian tube?
questions.explanation: Ciliary movement in the mucosa and peristaltic contractions propel the ovum toward the uterus.
questions.miniGuide: Ciliary movement in the mucosa and peristaltic contractions propel the ovum toward the uterus.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: Which function belongs to the vagina?
questions.explanation: The vagina serves as the passageway from the cervix to the exterior and functions as the birth canal.
questions.miniGuide: The vagina serves as the passageway from the cervix to the exterior and functions as the birth canal.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: What are the two central tasks of the female sexual cycle?

choices.D: Release an ovum and prepare the endometrium

questions.explanation: The cycle coordinates monthly ovum release with advance preparation of the uterine lining for implantation.
questions.miniGuide: The cycle coordinates monthly ovum release with advance preparation of the uterine lining for implantation.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: Why are the ovaries relatively inactive during childhood?

choices.A: Pituitary LH and FSH secretion is minimal

questions.explanation: Before puberty, low gonadotropin secretion provides little stimulation for ovarian cycling.
questions.miniGuide: Before puberty, low gonadotropin secretion provides little stimulation for ovarian cycling.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: What surrounds the ovum in a primordial follicle?

choices.B: A single layer of granulosa cells

questions.explanation: A primordial follicle contains an ovum surrounded by one layer of granulosa cells.
questions.miniGuide: A primordial follicle contains an ovum surrounded by one layer of granulosa cells.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: During the first days of the cycle, rising FSH primarily causes which change?

choices.B: Immediate formation of the corpus luteum
choices.C: Growth of a group of ovarian follicles

questions.explanation: FSH recruits and accelerates growth of several follicles early in the follicular phase.
questions.miniGuide: FSH recruits and accelerates growth of several follicles early in the follicular phase.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: What defines the antral stage of follicular development?

choices.A: Rupture of the mature follicular wall
choices.C: Conversion of the follicle into a corpus albicans
choices.D: Follicular fluid accumulates among granulosa cells

questions.explanation: Granulosa cells secrete fluid that collects to form the follicular antrum.
questions.miniGuide: Granulosa cells secrete fluid that collects to form the follicular antrum.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: How does estrogen promote accelerated growth of a developing follicle?

choices.A: It increases FSH receptors on granulosa cells
choices.D: It converts the follicle into scar tissue

questions.explanation: Estrogen increases granulosa-cell FSH receptors, making the follicle more responsive to FSH.
questions.miniGuide: Estrogen increases granulosa-cell FSH receptors, making the follicle more responsive to FSH.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: Why does one vesicular follicle usually outgrow the others?

choices.B: It becomes more responsive to gonadotropin stimulation
choices.D: It is isolated from the ovarian blood supply

questions.explanation: The dominant follicle gains a responsiveness advantage while the remaining follicles undergo atresia.
questions.miniGuide: The dominant follicle gains a responsiveness advantage while the remaining follicles undergo atresia.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: Which hormonal event is critical for ovulation?

choices.B: A fall in FSH during childhood

questions.explanation: The midcycle LH surge triggers the follicular changes that culminate in ovulation.
questions.miniGuide: The midcycle LH surge triggers the follicular changes that culminate in ovulation.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: Which event contributes directly to rupture of the mature follicle?

choices.B: Complete loss of follicular blood flow
choices.D: Proteolytic weakening of the follicular wall

questions.explanation: Proteolytic enzymes weaken the follicular wall while swelling and local vascular changes promote rupture.
questions.miniGuide: Proteolytic enzymes weaken the follicular wall while swelling and local vascular changes promote rupture.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: If the preovulatory LH surge does not occur, what is the most direct expected outcome?
questions.explanation: The LH surge is the essential trigger for ovulation, so its absence prevents release of the ovum.
questions.miniGuide: The LH surge is the essential trigger for ovulation, so its absence prevents release of the ovum.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: What structure forms from the remaining follicular cells after ovulation?
questions.explanation: Luteinized granulosa and thecal cells form the corpus luteum after the ovum is discharged.
questions.miniGuide: Luteinized granulosa and thecal cells form the corpus luteum after the ovum is discharged.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: Which hormone is secreted in especially large amounts by the corpus luteum?
questions.explanation: The corpus luteum is a major luteal source of progesterone and also secretes estrogen.
questions.miniGuide: The corpus luteum is a major luteal source of progesterone and also secretes estrogen.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: What normally happens to the corpus luteum when pregnancy does not occur?

choices.A: It enlarges throughout the next year
choices.B: It becomes a new dominant follicle
choices.C: It migrates into the fallopian tube

questions.explanation: Without pregnancy support, the corpus luteum involutes and is replaced by the corpus albicans.
questions.miniGuide: Without pregnancy support, the corpus luteum involutes and is replaced by the corpus albicans.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: How does early pregnancy prevent rapid loss of luteal hormone secretion?

choices.B: FSH converts it into an antral follicle

questions.explanation: Human chorionic gonadotropin maintains the corpus luteum so estrogen and progesterone secretion can continue.
questions.miniGuide: Human chorionic gonadotropin maintains the corpus luteum so estrogen and progesterone secretion can continue.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: Which follicular layer secretes steroid hormones during follicular development?
questions.explanation: The vascular theca interna contains steroid-secreting cells, while the theca externa is mainly connective tissue.
questions.miniGuide: The vascular theca interna contains steroid-secreting cells, while the theca externa is mainly connective tissue.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: What happens to vesicular follicles that do not become dominant?

choices.B: They become corpora lutea before ovulation

questions.explanation: One follicle becomes dominant while the remaining recruited follicles usually involute through atresia.
questions.miniGuide: One follicle becomes dominant while the remaining recruited follicles usually involute through atresia.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: From which precursor are ovarian steroid hormones derived?
questions.explanation: Ovarian estrogen and progesterone are steroid hormones synthesized from plasma-derived cholesterol.
questions.miniGuide: Ovarian estrogen and progesterone are steroid hormones synthesized from plasma-derived cholesterol.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: Why are androgens produced by theca cells important during the follicular phase?

choices.A: Granulosa cells convert them to estrogens

questions.explanation: Theca-derived androgens diffuse to granulosa cells, where aromatase converts them into estrogens.
questions.miniGuide: Theca-derived androgens diffuse to granulosa cells, where aromatase converts them into estrogens.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: FSH promotes estrogen synthesis in granulosa cells mainly by increasing which enzyme?
questions.explanation: FSH stimulates granulosa-cell aromatase, enabling conversion of theca-derived androgens to estrogens.
questions.miniGuide: FSH stimulates granulosa-cell aromatase, enabling conversion of theca-derived androgens to estrogens.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: How are estrogen and progesterone transported in plasma?
questions.explanation: As steroid hormones, they circulate largely associated with plasma proteins.
questions.miniGuide: As steroid hormones, they circulate largely associated with plasma proteins.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: Progesterone is metabolized primarily to which urinary product?
questions.explanation: The liver converts progesterone to pregnanediol, a portion of which is excreted in urine.
questions.miniGuide: The liver converts progesterone to pregnanediol, a portion of which is excreted in urine.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: During most of the cycle, estrogen and progesterone exert what effect on gonadotropin secretion?

choices.A: Negative feedback on LH and FSH
choices.B: Continuous stimulation of LH and FSH

questions.explanation: Outside the preovulatory interval, ovarian steroids mainly inhibit hypothalamic-pituitary gonadotropin output.
questions.miniGuide: Outside the preovulatory interval, ovarian steroids mainly inhibit hypothalamic-pituitary gonadotropin output.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: What makes the preovulatory feedback period unusual?

choices.B: High estrogen promotes a surge of LH

questions.explanation: Sustained preovulatory estrogen switches to positive feedback and promotes the LH surge.
questions.miniGuide: Sustained preovulatory estrogen switches to positive feedback and promotes the LH surge.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: After the corpus luteum involutes, why do LH and FSH begin to rise again?

choices.A: The endometrium releases large amounts of hCG
choices.D: The ovary becomes insensitive to all gonadotropins

questions.explanation: Loss of luteal estrogen and progesterone removes negative feedback, allowing gonadotropin secretion to recover.
questions.miniGuide: Loss of luteal estrogen and progesterone removes negative feedback, allowing gonadotropin secretion to recover.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: Which estrogen is identified as the most important estrogen in the lecture?
questions.explanation: Estradiol is presented as the principal estrogen responsible for many female reproductive effects.
questions.miniGuide: Estradiol is presented as the principal estrogen responsible for many female reproductive effects.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: What effect does estrogen have on the uterus during puberty?

choices.A: It enlarges the uterus and promotes endometrial growth
choices.D: It converts the uterus into fibrous tissue

questions.explanation: Estrogen supports growth of the uterus and proliferation of its endometrial lining.
questions.miniGuide: Estrogen supports growth of the uterus and proliferation of its endometrial lining.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: How does estrogen affect bone before epiphyseal closure?

choices.A: It prevents mineral deposition at all ages
choices.B: It stimulates growth, then closes the epiphyseal plates
choices.D: It stops osteoblast activity during puberty

questions.explanation: Estrogen contributes to the pubertal growth spurt and eventually promotes epiphyseal union.
questions.miniGuide: Estrogen contributes to the pubertal growth spurt and eventually promotes epiphyseal union.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: Which body-composition change is promoted by estrogen?

choices.C: Fat deposition in the breasts, hips, and thighs

questions.explanation: Estrogen supports the characteristic female fat distribution described in the lecture.
questions.miniGuide: Estrogen supports the characteristic female fat distribution described in the lecture.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: What is a major uterine action of progesterone?

choices.B: Cause menstrual shedding during the entire cycle
choices.C: Stimulate the preovulatory LH surge directly
choices.D: Promote secretory changes in the endometrium

questions.explanation: Progesterone converts the estrogen-primed endometrium into a secretory lining suitable for implantation.
questions.miniGuide: Progesterone converts the estrogen-primed endometrium into a secretory lining suitable for implantation.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: How does progesterone support pregnancy?

choices.A: It decreases the frequency and intensity of uterine contractions
choices.B: It increases uterine excitability throughout gestation
choices.D: It blocks development of breast lobules

questions.explanation: Progesterone quiets uterine contractility and helps maintain conditions favorable for pregnancy.
questions.miniGuide: Progesterone quiets uterine contractility and helps maintain conditions favorable for pregnancy.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: Which breast change is associated most directly with progesterone?
questions.explanation: Progesterone promotes lobular and alveolar development and prepares breast tissue for secretion.
questions.miniGuide: Progesterone promotes lobular and alveolar development and prepares breast tissue for secretion.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: What initiates menstruation when fertilization does not occur?
questions.explanation: Corpus-luteum regression lowers ovarian steroids, leading to vascular changes and shedding of the endometrium.
questions.miniGuide: Corpus-luteum regression lowers ovarian steroids, leading to vascular changes and shedding of the endometrium.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: Which event contributes to loss of the functional endometrium during menstruation?

choices.A: Permanent dilation of all uterine vessels

questions.explanation: Vasoconstriction and reduced perfusion promote tissue breakdown before the lining is expelled.
questions.miniGuide: Vasoconstriction and reduced perfusion promote tissue breakdown before the lining is expelled.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: Which hormone is mainly responsible for the proliferative phase of the endometrium?
questions.explanation: Follicular estrogen rebuilds and thickens the endometrium after menstruation.
questions.miniGuide: Follicular estrogen rebuilds and thickens the endometrium after menstruation.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: Which hormone drives the secretory phase of the endometrium?
questions.explanation: Luteal progesterone causes endometrial glands to become secretory and increases nutrient availability.
questions.miniGuide: Luteal progesterone causes endometrial glands to become secretory and increases nutrient availability.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: A failure of corpus-luteum progesterone secretion would most directly impair which uterine event?

choices.D: Ciliary movement within the fallopian tube

questions.explanation: The corpus luteum supplies the progesterone needed to convert proliferative endometrium into implantation-ready secretory tissue.
questions.miniGuide: The corpus luteum supplies the progesterone needed to convert proliferative endometrium into implantation-ready secretory tissue.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: What ovarian change characterizes menopause?

choices.C: Formation of a new corpus luteum each day

questions.explanation: As the remaining follicles become depleted or unresponsive, ovarian cycling and ovulation cease.
questions.miniGuide: As the remaining follicles become depleted or unresponsive, ovarian cycling and ovulation cease.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: Why do LH and FSH levels rise after menopause?

choices.B: Increased secretion of ovarian inhibiting hormones
choices.D: Continuous hCG release from the uterus

questions.explanation: Reduced estrogen and progesterone removes inhibitory feedback from the hypothalamic-pituitary axis.
questions.miniGuide: Reduced estrogen and progesterone removes inhibitory feedback from the hypothalamic-pituitary axis.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: Which change is associated with loss of estrogen after menopause?
questions.explanation: Estrogen loss reduces support for bone maintenance and contributes to declining bone strength.
questions.miniGuide: Estrogen loss reduces support for bone maintenance and contributes to declining bone strength.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: Which autonomic division primarily supports female erection and lubrication?
questions.explanation: Parasympathetic activity produces vasodilation and secretory responses involved in erection and lubrication.
questions.miniGuide: Parasympathetic activity produces vasodilation and secretory responses involved in erection and lubrication.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: What is a direct effect of nitric oxide during female arousal?

choices.A: Constriction of all genital blood vessels

questions.explanation: Nitric oxide promotes local vasodilation, increasing blood flow to erectile tissues.
questions.miniGuide: Nitric oxide promotes local vasodilation, increasing blood flow to erectile tissues.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: Why is the fertile period longer than the ovum's approximate 24-hour viability?

choices.A: Sperm may remain viable for several days
choices.B: The ovum remains fertile for a month

questions.explanation: Sperm survival before ovulation extends the interval during which intercourse can result in fertilization.
questions.miniGuide: Sperm survival before ovulation extends the interval during which intercourse can result in fertilization.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction

questions.question: How do estrogen-progestin contraceptives primarily suppress ovulation?

choices.A: They increase the preovulatory LH surge

questions.explanation: Exogenous ovarian steroids maintain feedback that suppresses gonadotropins and prevents the normal ovulatory surge.
questions.miniGuide: Exogenous ovarian steroids maintain feedback that suppresses gonadotropins and prevents the normal ovulatory surge.

metadata.source: FINAL WI 26 Week 13 Lecture - Female Reproduction
